data.cultural_impact: The name Joah carries a rich cultural history and is deeply rooted in the Hebrew Bible. In the Christian tradition, it is often associated with the biblical character John the Baptist, who prepared the way for Jesus Christ and was a significant figure in the Jewish community. The name Joah is also used in various Christian communities around the world and has become a beloved and meaningful name for many families.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Joah holds a deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the Hebrew name Yoḥanan, which means ‘God is gracious’. This name reminds us of God's unending love, mercy, and grace towards us. It serves as a reminder of the abundant blessings God bestows upon us and encourages us to live our lives in gratitude and love for Him. The name Joah is a constant reminder of the gentle and loving nature of God, and the faith and trust we can place in Him.

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament, the prophet Joah is mentioned as the son and successor of Jeroboam II, who reigned over Israel from about 782-746 BC. Joah continued his father's religious reforms, but was then accused of idolatry and was imprisoned by the priests of the golden calves at Bethel.

The New Testament mentions a man named Joah (or Jode) who was a disciple of Jesus and a Levite, likely from Galilee. He is mentioned in the Gospel of Matthew (10:3) as one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus to spread the word of God.
